segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have an upper intermediate level lesson for all of you.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为你们所有人准备了一节中高级课程。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We're going to be talking business on this occasion on EnglishPod but specifically about planning a business.
segments.zh: 这一次我们在 EnglishPod 上要聊的是商业，具体来说是规划创业。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So before a business opens, a lot of planning has to happen.
segments.zh: 因此，在企业开业之前，必须进行大量计划。

segments.en: That means people will decide what kind of a product they want to sell, what kind of a market they want to sell to, etc.
segments.zh: 这意味着人们将决定他们想销售什么样的产品，他们想卖给什么样的市场，等等。

segments.en: So that is the focus of today's lesson.
segments.zh: 所以这就是今天课程的重点。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to the dialogue for the first time and we'll be back in a minute to talk about what's going on.
segments.zh: 我们先听一遍对话，稍后回来聊聊发生了什么。

segments.en: I've had it.
segments.zh: 我受够了。

segments.en: I'm done working for a company that is taking me nowhere.
segments.zh: 我不想再给这家让我毫无发展前途的公司干了。

segments.en: So what are you going to do?
segments.zh: 那你打算怎么办？

segments.en: Just quit?
segments.zh: 直接辞职？

segments.en: That's exactly what I'm going to do.
segments.zh: 这正是我要做的。

segments.en: I've decided to create my own company.
segments.zh: 我决定创建自己的公司。

segments.en: I'm going to write up a business plan, get some investors and start working for myself.
segments.zh: 我将编写一个商业计划，吸引一些投资者并开始为自己工作。

segments.en: Have you ever written up a business plan before?
segments.zh: 你以前写过商业计划吗？

segments.en: Well, no.
segments.zh: 嗯，没有。

segments.en: It can't be that hard.
segments.zh: 应该没那么难吧。

segments.en: I mean, all you have to do is explain your business.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，你所要做的就是解释你的生意。

segments.en: How are you going to do things?
segments.zh: 你打算怎么做？

segments.en: And that's it, right?
segments.zh: 就这些了，对吧？

segments.en: You couldn't be more wrong.
segments.zh: 你可大错特错了。

segments.en: A well-written business plan will include an executive summary which highlights the idea of the business in two pages or less.
segments.zh: 一份写得很好的商业计划书会包含一份执行摘要，用两页或更少的篇幅概括业务构想。

segments.en: Then you need to describe your company with information such as what type of legal structure it has, history, etc.
segments.zh: 然后你要描述你的公司，包括它的法律结构类型、历史等信息。

segments.en: Well that seems easy enough.
segments.zh: 好吧，这似乎很容易。

segments.en: Wait, there's more!
segments.zh: 等等，还有更多！

segments.en: Then you need to introduce and describe your goods or services, what they are and how they're different from competitors.
segments.zh: 然后，您需要介绍和描述您的商品或服务，它们是什么以及它们与竞争对手的不同之处。

segments.en: Then comes the hard part, a market analysis.
segments.zh: 然后是困难的部分，市场分析。

segments.en: You need to investigate and analyse hundreds of variables.
segments.zh: 您需要调查和分析数百个变量。

segments.en: You need to take into consideration socio-economic factors from GDP per capita to how many children on average the population has.
segments.zh: 您需要考虑从人均 GDP 到人口平均有多少儿童的社会经济因素。

segments.en: All this information is useful so that you can move on to your strategy and implementation stage where you will describe in detail how you will actually execute your idea.
segments.zh: 所有这些信息都很有用，因此您可以进入您的战略和实施阶段，您将详细描述您将如何实际执行您的想法。

segments.en: Geez, is that all?
segments.zh: 哎呀，这就是全部吗？

segments.en: Almost.
segments.zh: 差一点。

segments.en: The most important piece of information for your investors will be the financial analysis.
segments.zh: 对您的投资者来说，最重要的信息将是财务分析。

segments.en: Here you will calculate and estimate sales, cash flow and profits.
segments.zh: 在这里，您将计算和估计销售额、现金流量和利润。

segments.en: After all, people will want to know when they will begin to see a return on their investment.
segments.zh: 毕竟，人们会想知道他们什么时候开始看到他们的投资回报。

segments.en: I think I'll just stick to my old job and save myself all the hassle of trying to start up a business.
segments.zh: 我想我会坚持我的旧工作，省去创业的所有麻烦。

segments.en: Alright we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So the guy wanted to open up a business but his friend explained that it's not so easy and gave a lot of interesting words and phrases there.
segments.zh: 所以这家伙想开一家公司，但他的朋友解释说这并不容易，并在那里给出了很多有趣的单词和短语。

segments.en: He did.
segments.zh: 确实如此。

segments.en: He seemed a little naive.
segments.zh: 他似乎有点天真。

segments.en: Like he didn't really know how much work is involved in opening a business.
segments.zh: 就像他真的不知道开办企业需要多少工作。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So I think we should take a look at some of the words used on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们应该看看语言要点中使用的一些单词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: The first word is the heart and soul of the process before you open a business.
segments.zh: 第一个词是创业前整个流程的核心。

segments.en: It's the business plan.
segments.zh: 这是商业计划。

segments.en: Alright so the business plan.
segments.zh: 好吧，商业计划。

segments.en: As you said it's a noun and it's basically a document that explains what's going on in the business.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，它是一个名词，它基本上是一个解释业务中正在发生的事情的文件。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: It's a paper that you write about the business that you want to open and it's a plan.
segments.zh: 这是你为自己想开的公司写的一份文件，它是一份计划。

segments.en: So that's what the name says.
segments.zh: 顾名思义。

segments.en: You have to tell what you will do, how much money you will spend, how much money you will need.
segments.zh: 你必须告诉你会做什么，你会花多少钱，你需要多少钱。

segments.en: Because if you're asking people for money, they want to know where the money will be spent if it's going to be spent on wise decisions.
segments.zh: 因为如果你向别人要钱，他们想知道这笔钱会花在哪里，是不是花在明智的地方。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And as you mentioned, you show this business plan maybe to a bank but also maybe to an investor.
segments.zh: 正如你提到的，你会把这份商业计划拿给银行看，也可能拿给投资者看。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So investor is our next word.
segments.zh: 所以投资者是我们的下一个词。

segments.en: It's another noun but this noun is a person.
segments.zh: 这是另一个名词，但这个名词是一个人。

segments.en: A person is an investor.
segments.zh: 投资者就是一个人。

segments.en: If he or she gives money to someone else and expects more money to come back.
segments.zh: 如果他或她把钱给别人，并期望更多的钱回来。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So a person that's starting out a business maybe has enough money himself to open up a business but sometimes you need extra money so you look for investors.
segments.zh: 因此，一个正在创业的人自己可能有足够的钱来创业，但有时你需要额外的钱，所以你要寻找投资者。

segments.en: People who are interested in giving you money.
segments.zh: 有兴趣给你钱的人。

segments.en: For example, I have a cupcake company.
segments.zh: 例如，我有一家纸杯蛋糕公司。

segments.en: I want to sell cupcakes to people and I need a thousand dollars.
segments.zh: 我想把纸杯蛋糕卖给人们，我需要一千美元。

segments.en: So Marco, do you want to be an investor?
segments.zh: 那么马可，你想成为一名投资者吗？

segments.en: Do you want to invest some money?
segments.zh: 你想投资一些钱吗？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: For sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: A cupcake company.
segments.zh: 一家纸杯蛋糕公司。

segments.en: That sounds great.
segments.zh: 听起来很棒。

segments.en: I know but what happens if I don't sell cupcakes?
segments.zh: 我知道但是如果我不卖纸杯蛋糕会怎样？

segments.en: That's a problem for you because you have made a risky investment.
segments.zh: 这对您来说是个问题，因为您进行了一项有风险的投资。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that's what happens with investors.
segments.zh: 所以这就是投资者的情况。

segments.en: But now if you want to attract the attention of your investors with your business plan, I think part of the most important aspects of this plan is the executive summary.
segments.zh: 但现在，如果您想通过您的商业计划来吸引投资者的注意力，我认为该计划最重要的部分是执行摘要。

segments.en: A summary is usually an outline of the important points of a paper or a document.
segments.zh: 摘要通常是对文章或文件要点的概述。

segments.en: So in this case I could say, Catherine's cupcake company will sell delicious cupcakes of 10 different flavors to the market of 5 year olds, 55 year olds.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我可以说，凯瑟琳的纸杯蛋糕公司将向 5 岁、55 岁的市场出售 10 种不同口味的美味纸杯蛋糕。

segments.en: People will love them.
segments.zh: 人们会爱他们。

segments.en: She has a great secret recipe and she plans to triple her investments by next year.
segments.zh: 她有一个很好的秘方，她计划到明年将她的投资增加三倍。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's exactly it.
segments.zh: 正是如此。

segments.en: So if an investor reads the executive summary, which shouldn't be more than two pages long, you can pretty much get the idea of what the business is about.
segments.zh: 因此，如果投资者阅读了不应该超过两页的执行摘要，您几乎可以了解业务的内容。

segments.en: So if you want more details, you have to read the rest of the business plan.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您想要更多详细信息，您必须阅读商业计划的其余部分。

segments.en: But mainly with the executive summary, you can more or less know what it's all about.
segments.zh: 但主要是通过执行摘要，您或多或少可以知道它的全部内容。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a summary, like I said, is something that should be short and it should give you all of the most important information about something.
segments.zh: 所以，就像我说的，摘要应该简短，它应该给你提供关于某事的所有最重要的信息。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And while they were talking more in depth about analyzing things and doing some research, and among those things, the girl mentioned the socio-economic factors.
segments.zh: 当他们更深入地谈论分析事物和进行一些研究时，在这些事情中，女孩提到了社会经济因素。

segments.en: Okay, when I said we're going to sell cupcakes from my company to people between the ages of 5 and 55, we need to analyze, we need to look at their socio-economic factors.
segments.zh: 好吧，当我说我们要把我公司的纸杯蛋糕卖给 5 到 55 岁的人时，我们需要分析一下，我们需要看看他们的社会经济因素。

segments.en: Socio comes from the word social.
segments.zh: Socio 来自 social 这个词。

segments.en: It means where in society they are, they're upper class, middle class or lower class.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们在社会的什么地方，他们是上层阶级、中产阶级或下层阶级。

segments.en: Economic means how much money do they make?
segments.zh: Economic 是指他们赚多少钱？

segments.en: Do they make $10,000 a year or $100,000 a year?
segments.zh: 他们每年赚 10,000 美元还是每年 100,000 美元？

segments.en: And so the kind of people we want to sell my cupcakes to will change according to their socio-economic factors.
segments.zh: 因此，我们想把我的纸杯蛋糕卖给的那种人会根据他们的社会经济因素而改变。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So as you mentioned, socio comes from the word social or from society.
segments.zh: 所以正如你提到的，socio 来自 social 这个词，或者说来自 society。

segments.en: So you're analyzing these factors from society.
segments.zh: 因此，您正在分析社会中的这些因素。

segments.en: And well, part of these factors is the GDP per capita.
segments.zh: 好吧，这些因素的一部分是人均 GDP。

segments.en: So we have two different words there.
segments.zh: 所以我们有两个不同的词。

segments.en: An acronym, GDP.
segments.zh: 缩写，GDP。

segments.en: GDP, gross domestic product.
segments.zh: GDP，国内生产总值。

segments.en: That might seem confusing because gross means different things at different times.
segments.zh: 这可能会让人困惑，因为 gross 在不同场合有不同意思。

segments.en: But in this case, domestic means our country.
segments.zh: 但在这里，domestic 指的是本国。

segments.en: So within a country, all of the products added up together.
segments.zh: 所以在一个国家，所有的产品加起来。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And gross is basically that.
segments.zh: gross 基本上就是这个意思。

segments.en: Just all the products added up together without taking into consideration any other things.
segments.zh: 只是所有的产品都加在一起，没有考虑任何其他事情。

segments.en: So the GDP is basically all the goods and services produced in a country within a given time.
segments.zh: 因此，GDP 基本上是一个国家在给定时间内生产的所有商品和服务。

segments.en: And what about per capita though?
segments.zh: 那么人均呢？

segments.en: So per capita comes from Latin.
segments.zh: 所以 per capita 来自拉丁语。

segments.en: Per means four or each.
segments.zh: per 表示“每一”或“每个”。

segments.en: And capita is a head.
segments.zh: capita 意思是“头”。

segments.en: So this is per person.
segments.zh: 所以这是人均。

segments.en: So GDP per capita means how much, how many goods and services are made divided by the number of people in that place.
segments.zh: 所以人均 GDP 就是把生产出的商品和服务总量除以那个地方的人口数。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you probably have these indicators in your country or your own language as well.
segments.zh: 因此，您可能在您的国家或您自己的语言中也有这些指标。

segments.en: But that's basically it.
segments.zh: 但基本上就是这样。

segments.en: And the acronym is gross domestic product.
segments.zh: 首字母缩写是国内生产总值。

segments.en: And just to explain a little bit, if you see this in Wikipedia or in an encyclopedia, normally a very low GDP per capita is $500, American dollars.
segments.zh: 稍微解释一下，如果你在维基百科或百科全书中看到这个，通常偏低的人均 GDP 是 500 美元。

segments.en: And a high one would be $35,000.
segments.zh: 而高的能到 35,000 美元。

segments.en: And that's usually per year, right?
segments.zh: 这通常是每年的，对吧？

segments.en: Because that's usually how it's taken into consideration.
segments.zh: 因为这通常是考虑到它的方式。

segments.en: The time is a year.
segments.zh: 时间是一年。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So those are the words that we have for you on language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以这些是我们在语言要点中为您准备的单词。

segments.en: Now why don't we move on to a couple of different phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 现在我们来看看流利表达里的几个短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is important.
segments.zh: 所以这很重要。

segments.en: First phrase, Marco, has to do with our last first phrase.
segments.zh: 第一个短语，Marco，与我们的最后一个短语有关。

segments.en: We had a business plan.
segments.zh: 我们有一个商业计划。

segments.en: So what do you do?
segments.zh: 那你怎么办？

segments.en: You write up a business plan.
segments.zh: 你写一个商业计划。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And that's a common way of saying to write or to create, to work on a business plan, to write up.
segments.zh: 这是写作或创建、制定商业计划、撰写的常见方式。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's something that we say that's very colloquial.
segments.zh: 所以这是我们所说的非常口语化的东西。

segments.en: Something that is very spoken.
segments.zh: 是非常口语化的说法。

segments.en: And I can't explain why we say it, but you'll sound very fluent if you say, I'm going to write up a business plan.
segments.zh: 我无法解释我们为什么这么说，但如果你说 I'm going to write up a business plan，听起来会非常地道。

segments.en: Or why don't you write up a business plan?
segments.zh: 或者你为什么不写一个商业计划？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it would be correct to say, I'm going to write a business plan or I have to write a business plan.
segments.zh: 所以说是正确的，我要写一个商业计划书，或者我必须写一个商业计划书。

segments.en: But if you use this phrase, I'm going to write up a business plan, it's more fluent, right?
segments.zh: 但如果你用这句话，我会写一个商业计划，它更流利，对吧？

segments.en: It's just more native-like.
segments.zh: 只是更地道一些。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And our next phrase is a return on investment.
segments.zh: 我们的下一个短语是投资回报。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So early we talked about investors.
segments.zh: 刚才我们谈到了投资者。

segments.en: The money that they invest is called an investment.
segments.zh: 他们投资的资金称为投资。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: These words are all very closely related.
segments.zh: 这些词都非常密切相关。

segments.en: And when Marco decided to give money to my cupcake business, he expects the money to come back and he expects more actually to come back than what he put in.
segments.zh: 当 Marco 决定给我的纸杯蛋糕生意投钱时，他期望这笔钱能收回来，而且实际上收回的比他投入的还多。

segments.en: So that's called a return on investment.
segments.zh: 所以这被称为投资回报。

segments.en: The money that's the difference.
segments.zh: 钱就是差别。

segments.en: So if he gives me a thousand dollars and I give him back $1,500 in a year, he made $500.
segments.zh: 所以如果他给我一千美元，我一年还给他 1,500 美元，他赚了 500 美元。

segments.en: That's amazing.
segments.zh: 太棒了。

segments.en: So that means it's a good return on his investment.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着他的投资回报率不错。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So that's the term that we use, a return on investment.
segments.zh: 这就是我们使用的术语，投资回报。

segments.en: So you don't say to return on investment, you see a return on investment.
segments.zh: 所以你不会说 to return on investment，你会说 see a return on investment。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: It's a thing, it's a number, it's a quantity.
segments.zh: 它是一个东西，它是一个数字，它是一个数量。

segments.en: It's something you can count.
segments.zh: 这是你可以数数的东西。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And well, in the end, after seeing that this business plan is not so easy, the guy said, you know what?
segments.zh: 好吧，最后，看到这个商业计划没那么容易，那家伙说，你知道吗？

segments.en: I'm not going to quit my job and just save myself the hassle.
segments.zh: 我不辞职了，给自己省点麻烦。

segments.en: What's a hassle?
segments.zh: 什么是麻烦？

segments.en: The hassle.
segments.zh: 麻烦。

segments.en: That's an interesting word.
segments.zh: 这是一个有趣的词。

segments.en: So if I'm going to save myself the hassle, a hassle is like the problem or the hard work that it involves.
segments.zh: 因此，如果我要为自己省去麻烦，那么麻烦就像问题或它所涉及的辛勤工作。

segments.en: It's a lot of trouble.
segments.zh: 这是很多麻烦。

segments.en: A lot of trouble.
segments.zh: 很多麻烦。

segments.en: So I was going to cook some dinner tonight, but I'm going to save myself the hassle of going to the grocery store and buying it and cooking it by just ordering food.
segments.zh: 所以今晚我本来想做点晚饭，但为了省去去杂货店买菜、做饭的麻烦，我干脆直接点外卖。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So that's a good example.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很好的例子。

segments.en: Instead of doing all the work of cooking, you just save yourself the hassle, pick up the phone and get food delivered to your house.
segments.zh: 与其做所有的烹饪工作，不如省去自己的麻烦，拿起电话，把食物送到你家。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you can change here, you can say save myself, save yourself, save his self.
segments.zh: 所以这里可以变，你可以说 save myself、save yourself、save himself。

segments.en: So you change that pronoun.
segments.zh: 所以你改变了那个代词。

segments.en: The pronoun.
segments.zh: 代词。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you can save yourself the hassle or I'm just going to save myself the hassle.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说 save yourself the hassle，或者说 I'm just going to save myself the hassle。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's about it for fluency builder.
segments.zh: 这就是流利表达的部分。

segments.en: Let's listen to today's dialogue one more time and we'll be back in a minute to talk about business.
segments.zh: 我们再听一遍今天的对话，稍后回来聊聊商业。

segments.en: I've had it.
segments.zh: 我受够了。

segments.en: I'm done working for a company that is taking me nowhere.
segments.zh: 我不想再给这家让我毫无发展前途的公司干了。

segments.en: So what are you going to do?
segments.zh: 那你打算怎么办？

segments.en: Just quit?
segments.zh: 直接辞职？

segments.en: That's exactly what I'm going to do.
segments.zh: 这正是我要做的。

segments.en: I've decided to create my own company.
segments.zh: 我决定创建自己的公司。

segments.en: I'm going to write up a business plan, get some investors and start working for myself.
segments.zh: 我将编写一个商业计划，吸引一些投资者并开始为自己工作。

segments.en: Have you ever written up a business plan before?
segments.zh: 你以前写过商业计划吗？

segments.en: Well, no, it can't be that hard.
segments.zh: 嗯，不会那么难吧。

segments.en: I mean, all you have to do is explain your business.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，你所要做的就是解释你的生意。

segments.en: How are you going to do things?
segments.zh: 你打算怎么做？

segments.en: And that's it, right?
segments.zh: 就这些了，对吧？

segments.en: You couldn't be more wrong.
segments.zh: 你大错特错了。

segments.en: A well-written business plan will include an executive summary, which highlights the idea of the business in two pages or less.
segments.zh: 一份写得很好的商业计划书将包括一份执行摘要，其中强调了两页或更少的业务理念。

segments.en: Then you need to describe your company with information such as what type of legal structure it has, history, etc.
segments.zh: 然后你要描述你的公司，包括它的法律结构类型、历史等信息。

segments.en: Well, that seems easy enough.
segments.zh: 好吧，这似乎很容易。

segments.en: Wait, there's more.
segments.zh: 等等，还有更多。

segments.en: Then you need to introduce and describe your goods or services, what they are and how they're different from competitors.
segments.zh: 然后，您需要介绍和描述您的商品或服务，它们是什么以及它们与竞争对手的不同之处。

segments.en: Then comes the hard part, a market analysis.
segments.zh: 然后是困难的部分，市场分析。

segments.en: You need to investigate and analyze hundreds of variables.
segments.zh: 您需要调查和分析数百个变量。

segments.en: You need to take into consideration socioeconomic factors from GDP per capita to how many children on average the population has.
segments.zh: 您需要考虑从人均 GDP 到人口平均有多少儿童的社会经济因素。

segments.en: All this information is useful so that you can move on to your strategy and implementation stage, where you will describe in detail how you will actually execute your idea.
segments.zh: 所有这些信息都很有用，以便您可以进入您的战略和实施阶段，您将在其中详细描述您将如何实际执行您的想法。

segments.en: Geez, is that all?
segments.zh: 哎呀，这就是全部吗？

segments.en: Almost.
segments.zh: 差一点。

segments.en: The most important piece of information for your investors will be the financial analysis.
segments.zh: 对您的投资者来说，最重要的信息将是财务分析。

segments.en: Here you will calculate and estimate sales, cash flow and profits.
segments.zh: 在这里，您将计算和估计销售额、现金流量和利润。

segments.en: After all, people will want to know when they will begin to see a return on their investment.
segments.zh: 毕竟，人们会想知道他们什么时候开始看到他们的投资回报。

segments.en: I think I'll just stick to my old job and save myself all the hassle of trying to start up a business.
segments.zh: 我想我会坚持我的旧工作，省去创业的所有麻烦。

segments.en: So it was pretty interesting that he wanted to quit his job and just, you know, set up a business.
segments.zh: 所以很有趣的是，他想辞掉工作，只是，你知道，创业。

segments.en: But actually, many people say that business plans are unnecessary.
segments.zh: 但实际上，许多人说商业计划是不必要的。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: Do these people have lots of money and they don't need investors?
segments.zh: 这些人有很多钱，不需要投资者吗？

segments.en: I think the problem is that there are many books out there that give you clear examples of companies, Fortune 500 companies, that started out without a business plan.
segments.zh: 问题在于，有很多书会给你举出一些活生生的例子，比如《财富》500 强公司，它们创业时就没有商业计划。

segments.en: So I think many people take this as a rule.
segments.zh: 所以我认为很多人都认为这是一项规则。

segments.en: A rule.
segments.zh: 一个规则。

segments.en: Like, well, they didn't need one or it's not really necessary or why should I write up a business plan?
segments.zh: 就像，好吧，他们不需要一个，或者这不是真正必要的，或者我为什么要写一份商业计划？

segments.en: Well, I'm not an entrepreneur and I'm not a business person, but my feeling is that a business plan is as much for investors as it is for yourself.
segments.zh: 好吧，我不是企业家，也不是商人，但我的感觉是，商业计划对投资者和对自己来说都是如此。

segments.en: It helps you clarify your goals.
segments.zh: 它可以帮助您明确您的目标。

segments.en: It helps you explain your objectives to your future colleagues.
segments.zh: 它可以帮助您向未来的同事解释您的目标。

segments.en: And I think it's just a really good way to map out the first year of a business because it tends to, a lot of businesses fail in that first year.
segments.zh: 而且我觉得这是规划企业第一年的好办法，因为——很多企业往往就是在第一年倒掉的。

segments.en: So I think this is a really important step.
segments.zh: 所以我认为这是一个非常重要的步骤。

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: So it's very interesting.
segments.zh: 所以这很有意思。

segments.en: We've talked a little bit about business here, but we would like to know your ideas or your comments or any other suggestions that you have about this topic or any topic on EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 我们在这里讨论了一些关于业务的信息，但我们想知道您的想法或意见或您对该主题或 EnglishPod 的任何主题的任何其他建议。

segments.en: So why don't you send us a comment or a personal message.
segments.zh: 那么您为什么不给我们发送评论或个人信息。

segments.en: We are at EnglishPod.com and we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 我们在 Englishpod.com，我们会在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: See you there.
segments.zh: 在那里见。
